expected_skill_registry_entries.statement: discriminator features are SUPPLIED evidence about the following word (its category, its mood exponent, its case exponent); the consumer never reads them off the shape, which is identical across every function
the statement negation leaves the verb's mood untouched; the prohibitive licenses the third mood. Mood is therefore the ONLY formal separator between them

for vowel-exponed verbs that separator is invisible in unvocalised text: `unvocalised_vowel_exponent` is declared as a licit value for BOTH functions, so such an occurrence yields two survivors and is preserved as alternatives — the undecidable outcome is a reportable result, not a failure
the categorical-negation function is a distinct regime keyed on an indefinite noun bearing nasb without tanwin; it is never reached from a verbal environment
exactly one survivor -> that function (candidate); more than one -> preserve_alternatives; none -> abstain insufficient_features. There is NO default function
the prohibitive is NOT restricted to the second person; a person feature is therefore never used to exclude it
this unit reports the function of the occurrence; it emits no mood assignment, no case assignment and no illocutionary claim beyond the named function
